item.title: [Itrfoundation] Nearly $1 Billion in Local Bonds on Iowa’s November Ballot
item.description:
Iowa voters will decide more than who represents them in public office this November. Across the state, local governments are asking voters to approve nearly $1 billion in borrowing, along with several tax and governance measures that could affect their communities for years to come.

According to Iowans for Tax Relief Foundation's review of the November 3,2026 ballots, there are 62 local public measures, including 44 general obligation and/or revenue bond questions, meaning that public debt accounts for the largest share of the ballot questions.  Together, local governments are seeking approximately $955 million in borrowing authority. Although both the number and total value of bond proposals are lower than in recent November elections, the amount remains substantially.  Additionally, 12 other tax measures, and six questions involving local government operations will also go before voters.

The post Nearly $1 Billion in Local Bonds on Iowa’s November Ballot appeared first on ITR Foundation.
